1rpxv5b: Cuanto más…, más…: two things that change together
1ez5yf4: To say that one thing increases or decreases at the same time as another, use two parts: «cuanto más / menos…» and then «más / menos / mejor / peor…». It takes no article and no «que»: «cuanto más se pedalea, más se conoce la ciudad», never «lo más… lo más». The subject usually goes after the verb: «cuanto más crece la ciudad…».
1wq73o5: «Cuanto» does not change before a verb, an adjective or an adverb, but it agrees with a noun: «cuanta más gente», «cuantos más árboles», «cuantas más bicicletas». With «mayor», «menor», «antes» or «después», «más» is not added: «cuanto mayor es el río…», «cuanto antes, mejor». In many Latin American countries you also hear «mientras más…, más…», with the same meaning.
1x0584v: The mood depends on time. For what is general, habitual or past, indicative: «Cuanto más llueve, más sube el río». For what is future or hypothetical, present subjunctive in the first part: «Cuanto antes empiecen las obras, antes estará el parque». In a past narrative about something that was future at the time, imperfect subjunctive: «Dijeron que cuanto más esperáramos, más caro saldría».
1d22o29: To talk about a single thing that changes over time, you do not need two parts: «cada vez más», «cada vez menos», «cada vez mejor» (never «cada vez más mejor»).

1gkjjph: Linking paragraphs: conceding without giving in
12ozdtc: In week 6 you reviewed «aunque», «a pesar de que» and «por mucho que» within a single sentence. Now the level is the text: connectors that link a sentence or a paragraph to the next. «Sin embargo» and «no obstante» (more formal) present a contrast: they go after a full stop or a semicolon, and take a comma after them. They can also go in the middle, between commas. Never «pero sin embargo».
tr192w: «Aun así», «con todo» and «así y todo» say that the result holds despite what came before. «De todas formas», «de todos modos» and «de todas maneras» indicate that, whatever the previous point, what follows holds. «Pese a» + noun or infinitive and «pese a que» are formal. In conversation, «y eso que» + indicative adds, after the main idea, a fact that would lead you to expect the opposite: «Llegó en bici, y eso que llovía».

1eez1dc: Objecting in a debate: ahora bien, eso sí and other phrases
1pdxg9c: «Ahora bien» accepts what has been said and opens an important objection or condition: «El parque es necesario. Ahora bien, ¿dónde estacionarán los feriantes?». «Eso sí» adds a condition or a nuance, often in a friendly tone: «Apoyo la ciclovía; eso sí, con buena iluminación». «Aunque» can work like «pero» to correct yourself: it always comes after and takes the indicative: «Me gusta el plan, aunque no me convence el plazo».
t60k4s: In an oral debate, conceding before objecting makes your position more convincing. The most useful phrases: «Tienes razón en que + indicative, pero…», «No digo que no + subjunctive, pero…», «Puede que tengas razón, pero…», «Es cierto que…; ahora bien…», «Ya, pero…» (colloquial).

1toosmp: Original SpanishCue text written as a feature in the fictional magazine «Campus Biobío». The project, the data and the people quoted are invented.
slep6j: Anyone walking along the banks of the Biobío today, a few blocks from the main square, comes across a curious image: one of the widest rivers in Chile flows behind a row of parked cars. The land, almost four hectares, was handed over to the council in 2019 and has worked as a free car park ever since. In March, the project to turn it into a park with a bike path and a wetland was approved by the city council, and that same month a public consultation was opened to collect submissions.
1dodizx: The response exceeded all expectations. More than nine hundred submissions were received in three weeks, so many that the deadline had to be extended to the end of the month. Residents, local market stallholders and the two nearby universities were consulted. According to the technical team, the more opinions are gathered before putting the works out to tender, the fewer changes will have to be made during the works, which is when changes cost more.
a52ck9: The arguments in favour are well known. The city has few green spaces by the water and, in summer, the centre gets so hot that many families look for shade outside the district. The fact that the most central riverbank is occupied by cars, the supporters say, shows that the city has turned its back on its river for decades. In addition, the wetland is not decoration: the more space the water has to spread out during floods, the less risk the low-lying neighbourhoods will face.
1qrvzb0: The objections, however, do not come only from those who defend the car. The shopkeepers on Barros Arana street are not against it because they distrust the park, but because their business depends on customers being able to load goods nearby. «I'm not saying a park isn't needed», a local hardware shop owner explained on Monday at the community centre, «but nobody remembered us when the plans were drawn». That same afternoon, the councillor in charge promised that she would go to listen to the shopkeepers the next day. She went; however, according to several witnesses, she forgot the plans and the meeting ended without specific agreements.
hayvua: There are also technical doubts. A civil engineering academic points out that the land floods almost every winter and that, therefore, the bike path will have to be built on an embankment. Even so, she considers the project viable. «It's more expensive than was said at first», she admits; «that said, the sooner it's done, the less it will cost, because construction prices keep going up».
1syjbp2: Despite the differences, in recent weeks a compromise has begun to take shape: keeping a loading and unloading zone in the street behind, planting more trees than planned and opening the park in stages. It is nobody's proposal in particular, even though nobody presented it as such. Perhaps that is the lesson of this consultation: the more you listen before deciding, the less you have to correct afterwards.
